title: One sip
invitation: Have a mouthful of water, whenever you next move.
detail: Not a glass. A mouthful. Dehydration makes everything harder to think through and it is the easiest thing on this list to fix.

title: Cold water on your wrists
invitation: Run cold water over the inside of your wrists for thirty seconds.
detail: This is the fastest way to bring a spiked nervous system down without having to think or decide anything. Face works too, if you can.

title: Longer out than in
invitation: Breathe in for four, out for eight. Six rounds.
detail: The long exhale is the part that does the work. Counting is optional if counting is annoying today.

title: Something heavy on you
invitation: Put something with weight across your lap or chest for a few minutes.
detail: A blanket, a cushion, a cat if one is available. Deep pressure tells the body it is contained.

title: Take the lights down
invitation: Turn off the overhead light and use a lamp, or nothing at all.
detail: Overhead light is the single most common unnoticed source of sensory load indoors.

title: Ears off for ten minutes
invitation: Put in ear defenders, loops or headphones with nothing playing.
detail: Silence is a different thing from quiet music. Ten minutes of actual silence can reset a whole afternoon.

title: Name five things
invitation: Look around and name five things you can see. Out loud or in your head.
detail: Not to fix anything. Just to put you back in the room you are actually in.

title: Lie on the floor
invitation: Get on the floor for five minutes. That is the whole thing.
detail: No stretching, no breathing exercise, no app. The floor holds you up so nothing else has to.

title: Two minutes only
invitation: Set a timer for two minutes on the thing you are avoiding, and stop when it goes.
detail: You are allowed to stop. The point is starting, and starting is the part that is actually hard.

title: Do it near someone
invitation: Do the task with another person in the room, or on a video call, doing their own thing.
detail: Body doubling. Nobody has to talk or help. Presence alone does something that willpower does not.

title: One surface
invitation: Clear one surface. Not the room. One surface.
detail: Pick the smallest one you can see. A visible finished thing is worth more than a plan.

title: Let a coin decide
invitation: For the next low-stakes decision you are stuck on, flip for it.
detail: When decision fatigue has set in, the cost of choosing badly is usually far lower than the cost of not choosing.

title: Write it anywhere
invitation: Put the thing you are trying not to forget somewhere outside your head. Anywhere.
detail: Back of your hand, a voice note, a text to yourself. Working memory is not a storage system and pretending otherwise costs you all day.

title: Close all but one
invitation: Close every tab, window and app except the one you need.
detail: Not for tidiness. Every open thing is a small pull on attention you are paying for without noticing.

title: Walk while you think
invitation: If a thought will not resolve sitting still, move while you have it.
detail: Pacing counts. Some brains genuinely process better in motion, and sitting still to concentrate is advice written for other people.

title: Set one anchor
invitation: Before you go in deep, set one alarm for something you must not miss.
detail: Hyperfocus is not the problem. Losing the thing on the other side of it is.

title: Say it flat
invitation: Describe what is happening in the most boring words you can find.
detail: "My chest is tight and my thoughts are fast" rather than "I am falling apart". Same facts, much less to carry.

title: Check the floor under it
invitation: Before anything else: have you eaten, drunk, slept, and taken what you take?
detail: Not a telling-off. Four physical things account for a startling share of what feels like emotional collapse.

title: Ninety seconds
invitation: When the wave hits, set ninety seconds and just let it be there.
detail: You do not have to do anything with it or about it. Most surges of feeling crest and start to drop in about that long.

title: Say the shame part
invitation: Say the bit you are most embarrassed about out loud, to yourself, once.
detail: Shame gets most of its weight from being unsaid. This is not confession and nobody has to hear it.

title: Ten minutes unmasked
invitation: For ten minutes, drop the performance. Stim, slump, stare, script nothing.
detail: Alone, door shut. Masking is genuine physical work and this is the only rest from it.

title: One true thing about today
invitation: Write one sentence about today that is true and not a judgement.
detail: "I got through a meeting I was dreading" counts. "I should have done more" does not — that is a verdict, not a fact.

title: Draft the ask
invitation: Write the message you are dreading, and do not send it yet.
detail: Writing it and sending it are two separate jobs. Doing the first one today makes the second one much smaller.

title: One sentence, no apology
invitation: Write your boundary as one sentence with no "sorry" and no explanation.
detail: You can add the softening back afterwards if you want it. Start from the version that is just true.

title: Tell one person a real thing
invitation: Tell one person one honest thing about how you actually are.
detail: Not everyone. One. It can be small and it does not have to lead anywhere.

title: Decide your exit first
invitation: Before the social thing, decide when you are leaving and how.
detail: Having an exit makes it possible to be there at all. Deciding it in advance means not negotiating with yourself while depleted.

title: Note where you are in the month
invitation: Log roughly where you are in your cycle, alongside how today felt.
detail: A few weeks of this and the pattern usually becomes obvious. Until then it just looks like being unreliable.

title: Lower the bar on purpose
invitation: Pick one thing this week that gets the minimum version, decided in advance.
detail: Choosing where to do less is different from running out of capacity and failing at everything at once.

title: Check pain before mood
invitation: Before you decide how you feel, rate any physical pain out of ten.
detail: Persistent low-level pain reliably reads as low mood or irritability, and it is treated very differently.

title: Three bullets for the appointment
invitation: Write the three things you must say, in order, before you go.
detail: Under pressure the important one is the one that goes missing. On paper it cannot.

title: Name one adjustment
invitation: Name one specific thing that would make work or study easier. Just name it.
detail: "A written summary after meetings" is askable. "More support" is not. Naming it is most of the work.

title: Book the recovery, not just the meeting
invitation: Put ten empty minutes in the diary straight after the demanding thing.
detail: The cost of the meeting is not the meeting. It is the hour afterwards you had already promised to something else.

title: Say the deadline to someone
invitation: Tell one person what you are doing and by when.
detail: External structure does what internal intention cannot, and this is the cheapest version of it.

title: Note what worked
invitation: Write down the thing that helped today, so you have it next time.
detail: You will not remember. Everyone assumes they will and nobody does.

title: Take the credit
invitation: Say what you did today and leave out the word "just".
detail: "I just replied to some emails" and "I replied to some emails" describe the same day very differently.

title: Get absorbed in one thing
invitation: Do one thing you like for its own sake, without checking how it is going.
detail: Not productive, not measured, not posted. The point is being in it.
